review.finding: Windows arm's spawnSync had no maxBuffer (asymmetric with the POSIX fix applied 20 lines below), and dropping the Where-Object clause increased pipe volume.
review.disposition: fixed — added maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024, symmetric with the POSIX arm.

review.finding: filterTsxEntriesByRepo's trailing-boundary anchor does not also anchor the leading edge, so a repoRoot that recurs verbatim as a subpath of a different absolute path (e.g. a POSIX bind mount) could still false-match.
review.disposition: investigated a leading-boundary anchor; reverted — in real command lines the absolute path is preceded by a quote/space/file:/// scheme, never reliably a bare separator, so requiring one broke genuine matches (all 51 tests). Accepted as a documented trade-off (JSDoc updated); Windows is immune by construction (drive letter can't recur mid-path); this exact scenario (identical repo path recurring under a POSIX bind-mount prefix) is outside the bug report's scope.

summary: Re-review confirmed all 3 substantive findings (unanchored substring match, execSync maxBuffer, duplicated tsx predicate) are structurally fixed, verified by hand-tracing every fixture plus independent end-to-end validation against real live tsx-watch processes across two worktrees (exact PID sets, zero cross-contamination). Both remaining low findings dispositioned above. PASS.
